segments.text:
WHen muche people were gathered together, & were come to hym out of all cyties, he ſpake by a ſimilytude. The ſower went out to ſowe his ſede: and as he ſowed, ſome fell by the way ſide, and it was troden doune, and the foules of the ayre deuoured it vp. And ſome fell on ſtones, & aſſone as it was ſprong vp, it withered away, becauſe it lacked moiſtnes. And ſome fell among thornes, and the thornes ſprāg vp with it & choked it. And ſome fel on good ground, and ſprang vp and bare fruite an hundreth folde. And as he ſayed theſe thinges, he cryed: he that hath eares to heare, let hym heare. And his diſciples aſked hym, ſaying: what mane• of ſimilitude is this? And he ſayed: vnto you it is geuen to knowe the ſecretes of the kingdome of God: but to other by parables, that whē they ſee, they ſhould not ſee, & when they heare, they ſhould not vnderſtand. The parable is this: The ſede is the worde of God: thoſe that are beſide the way, are they that heare: thē cometh the deuyll and taketh away the worde out of their
heartes, leſte they ſhould beleue and be ſaued. They on the ſtones, are they which when they heare, receiue the worde with ioy: & theſe haue no rootes, which for a while beleue, and in time of temptacion go awaye. And that which fell among thornes, are they which when they haue heard, go furth, and are choked with cares and ryches, and voluptuous lyuyng, and bring furth no fruite. That whiche fell in the good grounde, are they whiche with a pure and good heart, heare the worde and kepe it, and bryng furth fruite through pacience.
